The ground this stake farms, measured from it. Drawn on the ground while this window is open. A keep-out circle on the world map cuts a piece back out of it - that is how a field gets a shape that is not a circle.
This field takes {0} and its seed turn and turn about, so it makes its own seed and never asks for more.

Who may give this settlement orders. A Leader has your authority over everything the settlement does - trades, work, stores, land, trade routes - except two things: a Leader cannot give or take this title, and cannot hand the stone on. Only you can do those, because you raised it.
Nobody else is here to name.
Only the player who raised this Bảo Hộ (Frith)stone gives and takes titles here.
Lays a blueprint out as a plan. What it marks, the frith raises.
A roof and a lit fire. Small things, but they count.
Warm in here. I could stay a while.
A hot meal makes any day better.
Whoever cooked that has my thanks.
They struck the Bảo Hộ (Frith)stone. The stone itself.
If that fire goes out, none of the rest of it means anything.
I keep looking at the treeline. Cannot help it.
That was closer than I would like to admit.
I missed a meal and my stomach has not forgiven me.
Is anyone actually cooking, or is that just decoration?
I have eaten better on a hunt in the rain.
There is a place at the table nobody sat in tonight.
I keep expecting to hear them come round the corner.
We buried one of our own. I have nothing else to say today.
I barely closed my eyes last night.
Whoever is snoring by the fire owes me a night's rest.
I am running on nothing but stubbornness today.
Still finding my way around the place.
New stone, new start. We will see.
I would give a great deal for a bed of my own.
Sleeping on the floor again. My back has opinions.
Is there truly no room for one more bunk?
Slept like a stone. Do not wake me twice.
A proper night's rest and the world looks different.
I am not much use with empty hands.
Give me something to work with and I will earn my keep.
I feel half dressed without a proper tool.
They came through the gate. Through it.
I can see daylight where the wall used to be.
Whoever is rebuilding that, I will carry the wood.
Stood out there all night. Saw nothing. Good.
No sleep, but no trouble either. I will take that trade.
The caravan's load is still on the dock. We have nowhere to put it - build us a chest.
Goods came in and there they sit. Every chest we have is full.
My things. Right where I fell.
Took some finding, but it is all here.
It is over. Check the walls, someone.
That is enough excitement for one day.
I was stuck fast. Do not ask me how.
Back on solid ground. That will do.
I am getting the hang of this.
Better than I was last season, at least.
That was no kind of night.
I am awake. That is the most I will promise.
Now that is how a night should go.
Right. Let us get on with it.
This place is starting to feel like home.
A calm day is never wasted.
I have no complaints worth making.
Good company, decent food. What else is there?
I am not sure how much more of this I can take.
Nobody here seems to notice how bad it has got.
Some days I wonder why I stayed at all.
I have stopped expecting the day to improve.
Ordinary day. I will take ordinary.
Nothing broke, nothing burned. Good enough.
The work gets done either way.
It has been a rough stretch, I will say that.
I could do with something going right for once.
I am tired in a way sleep does not fix.
We are managing. Only just, mind you.
I would not trade this for a hall in Asgard.
Everything is where it should be for once.
I woke up glad to be here. Strange feeling.
We have built something worth keeping.
Something killed me out there. Somebody had better go and see.
I did not walk back from that ground. Take a spear if you go.
It came at me while I was working. It is still out there.
Someone should really organise that chest.
The kiln needs feeding again already.
A frith marches on its stomach.
I need more than roots to work with.
The soil out there is better than it looks.
Another few days and those will be ready.
The berries are coming in well this season.
I found mushrooms where there were none last week.
Quiet watch. That is how I like them.
I walked the wall twice. Nothing out of place.
Tracks by the stream. Deer, and recent.
The forest was unusually quiet this morning.
There is always more wood to cut.
That old birch out east is next, I reckon.
My arms remember every swing of that pick.
There is good stone in that outcrop yet.
Let them come. I would rather meet it than wait for it.
Fear is just something you do afterwards.
There is always more to be done before dark.
Idle hands make a poor frith.
I have been thinking about supper since breakfast.
Is that stew? Do not answer if it is not.
Takes more than a cold night to slow me down.
I have walked off worse than this.
The work will still be there tomorrow.
No sense hurrying. Nothing is chasing me.
It is good to hear voices about the place.
Stay and talk a while, the work can wait.
I do my best thinking with nobody talking at me.
Company is fine. In small amounts.
I would rather be behind the wall than in front of it.
Does anyone else hear that, or is it only me?
I have done this long enough to do it in my sleep.
There is a knack to it. Took me long enough to find.
Show me where. We will go and stand over it.
Then it will meet the watch next, not you.
Somebody in this settlement already answers to that.

A fisherman cannot make what it fishes with. Put a rod in a chest they are allowed to draw from, and moor a boat near the stone in water deep enough to float it - a hull dragged up onto a beach is no use to anybody, and they will stand there telling you they have no boat while it sits in the sand behind them.

From the day they take it out it is the settlement's boat. Should the sea walk it off while nobody is aboard, it will be found and brought back to its mooring. Take the helm yourself and it is yours again, and it goes where you go.

A guard has fallen on watch, and the peace with them. Until the attack is over, every resident who can fight will stand on the ground they work.

When the last foe is gone the frith mends itself. The fallen return to the stone in time, and go looking for what they left in their grave. Do not bury what you need.

They have gone. Two or three of your own, walking at the pace the road allows - and it allows what you built into it.

Do not wait on them. They keep walking whether you watch or sleep, and they will find the other hearth without you. Go and meet them on the way if you like the look of it. Nothing is bought and nothing sold: both halls are yours, and this is carrying, not trade.

Every chest within the walls belongs to the settlement. Hold shift and use one and you may say what it is for: which crafts draw their supplies from it, and what it should hold - the metal here, the meal there. The caretaker keeps to what you say and carries off whatever does not belong.

And what they hold is yours as well. Stand inside your own walls and build, and the chests answer for the cost without your opening a single one of them.

A chest for what leaves and what comes. Nobody here will touch it: not the caretaker who tidies everything else, not the hungry, not you when you build. What you set in it is what the next caravan carries, and what one brings is waiting in it.

Raise one at the far end too. A load must have somewhere to be set down, or it does not go.

This one is not the settlement's. It is yours. It will leave the wall behind, cross water with you, go through a portal and down into the dark, and it needs no bed and eats out of its own pack.

Hold shift and use them to say come or wait. Three tempers to choose between - stand and guard, go and hunt, or keep their hands down - and choose with care: the passive will not save you, and the eager will find you a fight you did not want.
One who walks out with you

A hall is not held by its walls. Your people need a bed of their own under a roof, food in a chest they are allowed to take from, and a wall that stands - and whichever of those you fail to give them shows in their face at the end of the day.

The stone will tell you which it was: slept badly, missed supper, no bed at all, a friend lost. Mend it and the reckoning goes back to nothing. Leave it, and one morning you will look for them and find them gone. They will have warned you first.

A builder does not invent. Show it what to make: take up the builder's hammer, look at something you have already raised, and press the key to write it down. It is a plan from that moment - no reloading, no waiting.

Set a plan on the ground and it stands as a ghost until the builder has paid for every piece of it out of the settlement's chests. Mending is its other half: it walks your walls and makes good what the night broke.

A stranger sits at your fire now. Give them a bed of their own within the walls, and chests to keep what they gather - they eat from those chests, and a hungry worker is a poor one.

Use the stone and you will find them there, waiting for a craft: the axe, the rod, the bow, or the watch. A village is made of small things, done every day.

There. A stretch of it is made, and it has gone green on your map - that is the ground answering, not me. Lay it in stone and it pales further, and a laden traveller walks quicker on stone than on packed earth.

Take your people out with you and it goes three times as fast. They will fell what stands in the way and go back to their crafts when you are done with them. And mark what the road is worth: over a bare line your goods go on backs and little of it goes at all. A road made end to end carries six times as much.

So. You have raised a Bảo Hộ (Frith)stone. Mark this before anything else: a frith is an enclosure. Raise walls around the stone and a gate to pass them, for what lies within the wall is yours and ordered, and what lies without is the wild. Your people will treat the wall as the edge of their world - they shelter behind it, and they defend it.

Only then bring coin to the stone and take someone in. A stone with no wall is a fire in the open, and the open belongs to the greydwarves.

They will carry wood until the wood is gone, if nobody ever says otherwise. Set what the settlement wants of a thing and they will work up to that and stop - and what is held below its mark is not eaten, so a store you are keeping stays kept.

Ask for nothing and they will judge it themselves. They are willing. They are not thrifty.

You have given them work. Now give them ground. On the map you may draw the circles they may work in, and the ones they must keep out of. Plant patrol points, and a guard will walk between them.

What you do not draw, they will decide for themselves - and they are not always wise.

The night has teeth. Hear me: the settlement's fight belongs to the guards. The cook, the woodcutter and the fisher keep to their work and out of the way, as they should.

Only if a guard falls does the frith break, and then every hand that can hold a blade defends its own ground. So arm your guards well, and give them a bed near the wall.

Two hearths, and nothing but wild between. You have asked where a road could run, and I have walked it for you: off the water, out of the mountains, round anything a laden traveller would turn an ankle on. It is a line, nothing more. No stone has been turned.

Follow it with a hoe. What you lay, I will count.

Built from Valheim's own character parts. What you choose is kept, shared with everyone in the world, and survives a death.

While you are standing in the settlement, what its chests hold counts towards what you are building, the same chests the Caretaker works out of. Turn it off if another mod already builds from containers - two of them fetching for one build is one fetch too many. This client only.
